## What is an agent?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A language model that calls tools, and loops until a check passes
- The harness runs the tools and builds the context
- Tools are things like a shell, file editing, GitHub, web search or a
  Julia session
- The context is everything the model sees, from instructions and skills
  to the conversation and tool results

::: {.column width="60%"}
![](figures/agents-tool-llm.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A coding agent. A language model, at a provider or local, reads
context and writes text or tool calls. A harness such as Claude Code
builds the context window from instructions, skills, the conversation
and tool results, runs each tool call in a shell, GitHub, web search or
an MCP server such as a Julia session, and puts the result back into the
context, repeating until done. The harness and tools run on your
computer, in the cloud or on an HPC cluster, which sets the agent's data
access, tools and compute. You give the prompt and read the answer."}

## Agents working together

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A lead agent dispatches subagents in parallel
- Each subagent has its own context and tools
- Only a summary comes back
- Workflow scripts make the dispatch repeatable
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](figures/agents-multi.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Two ways agents work together. On the left, a lead agent sends
tasks to implement, test and review subagents that run in parallel, each
with its own context and tools, and each returns only a summary. On the
right, a workflow script runs a fixed pipeline. Reviewers for bugs, tests
and docs run in parallel, a verifier checks each finding, and the
results are merged."}

::: {.attribution}
Anthropic 2025,
[How we built our multi-agent research system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)
:::
